title: Top K Frequent Elements
description:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` most frequent elements. You may return the answer in **any order**.

It is guaranteed that the answer is **unique** (there is no frequency tie separating the `k`-th most frequent element from the `(k + 1)`-th most frequent element).

Your algorithm's time complexity must be better than `O(n log n)`, where `n` is the array's size.
constraints: k is in the range [1, the number of unique elements in the array].
It is guaranteed that the answer is unique.
hints: First count the frequency of every distinct value in nums using a hash map in O(n) time.
Maintain a min-heap of size at most k keyed by frequency so you can discard less-frequent elements in O(log k) time each.
Alternatively, bucket sort by frequency (from 1 to n) achieves O(n) time.

examples.explanation: 1 appears 3 times, 2 appears 2 times, and 3 appears 1 time. The 2 most frequent elements are 1 and 2.
Only one unique element exists, so return [1].
-1 appears 3 times and 4 appears 2 times, while 2 and 0 each appear once.
